audit.why: phases[].side and win[] already agree row for row (Skill / Sylas / Skill / Sylas / Skill / Skill / Skill) and match both the packet chart and the already-audited mirror nasus__sylas. Sylas owns levels 2 and 4-5 where the burst-heal beats a Nasus who has no way to end a trade; the late rows correctly go neutral-to-negative as stacks arrive.
audit.corrected: No chart edits — leaving it matched.

audit.why: Four spikes, correctly ordered: level 2 Kingslayer, levels 4-5 passive chain-autos, level 6 Hijack, and the late stacked-Nasus stat check. Only the level 6 entry's description of what Hijack does was wrong.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields (whys[4], spikes[2].text, mid) claim Hijack strips Fury of the Sands from Nasus — 'while he fights a shrunken kit', 'stripping it from him', 'while he loses it'. Four fields also say Abduct stuns.
audit.why: Sylas's R steals a copy of the enemy ultimate and casts it freely; it does not disable or remove the enemy's own ultimate. A player told Nasus loses his R will all-in a Nasus who is about to press it. Abduct is a recast chain that pulls Sylas to the target, sharing Abscond's 13/12/11/10/9s cooldown, with no stun — the mirror audit reached the same conclusion.
audit.corrected: Hijack described as a copy, with the all-in gated on Nasus's own R being down (120/100/80s); stun claims removed.
sources: brief ownerKit R and E text

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns that Fury of the Sands does percent-max-health damage, so buying resistances is the wrong answer to his ultimate.
audit.why: The missingInteractions entry flags resistances-invalidated on Fury of the Sands, and the kit carries the percentHealth flag; stacking armour against a stacked Nasus does nothing about the storm itself.
audit.corrected: Moved into wants.you[1] as the reason to force the fight early.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention that Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: The Q's wind-up, not the cast, is the moment to back out; the missingInteractions entry flags it and the kit carries the autoReset flag.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are your window to convert poke into a real lead — weave passive chain-autos between every Q and W cast so your damage compounds without giving him a clean Wither angle. The key discipline is Wither management: the moment you see the animation, use E1 to dash forward (closing distance kills the kite) or eat it, then E2-hook back out before the slow cripples your attack speed on his counter-trade. At level 6 Hijack changes everything — steal Fury of the Sands and you gain his size and lifesteal while he loses it. Run the all-in immediately after stealing: you have his ultimate, your W heal, and he has nothing but a shrunken kit and a long Wither cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are your window to convert poke into a real lead — weave passive chain-autos between every Q and W cast so your damage compounds without giving him a clean Wither angle. The key discipline is Wither management: it is a 700-range point-and-click on an 11-15s cooldown, so the moment you see the cast, use E1 to dash forward (closing distance kills the kite), then E2-hook back out before the attack-speed decay ruins your counter-trade. At level 6 Hijack copies Fury of the Sands rather than taking it — you gain the health, resists and percent-health burn, and so does he if he presses his own. Run the all-in while his 120s R is still down.
